question: Where is the abnormal impulse generated, if in the electrocardiogram we observe an inverted P wave, but the QRS complex and the T wave are normal ?:
analysis: An inverted P wave in the electrocardiogram typically indicates that the impulse is originating from a location other than the sinoatrial (SA) node. When the P wave is inverted and the QRS complex and T wave are normal, it suggests that the impulse is being generated from the atrioventricular (AV) node or nearby areas. This is because the impulse is traveling in a retrograde direction towards the atria, causing the inversion of the P wave. The normal QRS complex and T wave indicate that ventricular depolarization and repolarization are occurring normally, which is consistent with an impulse originating from the AV node.
